B. Is this measure already running in Kainuu wellbeing services county (or in the OYS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Travel and accommodation support for patients far from the university hospital. Patients who must travel for surgery or weeks of radiotherapy get a booked patient hotel, organised transport and a named contact, so that distance is not the reason to choose a non-curative treatment.
supported_en: A 2009 registry study of 34,923 patients in northern England (British Journal of Cancer) found that patients with the longest travel time had 0.60 times the odds of lung cancer surgery.
not_supported_en: No page shows that travel or accommodation support raises the share of patients treated with curative intent, so the assumed 1 percentage point is not measured.
in_use_quote: Jos tulet pitkän matkan takaa eikä vointisi ole sellainen, että sinun tarvitsisi jäädä sairaalan vuodeosastolle, sinä ja läheisesi voitte majoittua sairaalan lähellä sijaitsevassa potilaskodissa.
missing_en: No page shows organised transport or a named contact who books accommodation for the patient. Patients book the room themselves.
summary_en: OYS runs a patient home in Oulu, 400–700 m from the hospital, with 32 + 31 beds at €41.98 per adult per night, and Kela pays back part of the cost. Kainuu's cancer care pathway pages tell radiotherapy patients to use it and to book it in advance, but patients book it themselves by phone, and no page shows organised transport or a named contact. For the effect, the only evidence is an association from England (odds of surgery 0.60 for the longest travel time); no study of a support measure was read.
unanswered_en: I found no Kainuu or OYS page on organised transport or a named travel coordinator for cancer patients, and no study of how much travel support changes curative treatment rates.
